status: PROPOSED. Frozen before any service observation; no table exists yet.
expectation_basis: Rows are synthetic and chosen here. Every expected result below was written by hand from these rows and the stated PostgreSQL semantics, then cross-checked by tests/test_db_fixture_package.py against an independent Python evaluation of the rows. No expected value was obtained by running SQL.
semantics_sources: PostgreSQL 14 manual, ORDER BY: ASC places NULLs last by default; NULLS LAST is stated explicitly anyway (https://www.postgresql.org/docs/14/queries-order.html)
PostgreSQL 14 manual, text equality is exact and case-sensitive; trailing spaces are significant for text (https://www.postgresql.org/docs/14/datatype-character.html)
PostgreSQL 14 manual, json_agg/json_build_object; date values are rendered in ISO 8601 in JSON (https://www.postgresql.org/docs/14/functions-json.html)

row_purposes.INV-05: case variant of the customer; must not match 'acme'
row_purposes.INV-11: trailing-space variant of the customer; must not match 'acme'
row_purposes.INV-02, INV-07: same customer, non-open status; excluded by the status filter
row_purposes.INV-03, INV-08: equal due_date; order is defined only by the invoice_key tie-break
row_purposes.INV-04: open acme invoice with no due date; NULLS LAST keeps it off the first page
row_purposes.INV-03, INV-04, INV-09: empty string versus NULL note, and NULL due_date, preserved distinctly

statements.fixture_write: BEGIN; CREATE SCHEMA harness_fixture; CREATE TABLE harness_fixture.invoices (invoice_key text PRIMARY KEY, customer text NOT NULL, status text NOT NULL CHECK (status IN ('open', 'paid', 'void')), amount_cents integer NOT NULL, due_date date, note text); INSERT INTO harness_fixture.invoices (invoice_key, customer, status, amount_cents, due_date, note) VALUES ('INV-01', 'acme', 'open', 12000, DATE '2026-11-05', NULL), ('INV-02', 'acme', 'paid', 8000, DATE '2026-10-01', 'paid early'), ('INV-03', 'acme', 'open', 4500, DATE '2026-10-20', ''), ('INV-04', 'acme', 'open', 4500, NULL, NULL), ('INV-05', 'ACME', 'open', 9900, DATE '2026-10-15', NULL), ('INV-06', 'globex', 'open', 30000, DATE '2026-10-18', NULL), ('INV-07', 'acme', 'void', 1000, DATE '2026-10-10', NULL), ('INV-08', 'acme', 'open', 7000, DATE '2026-10-20', NULL), ('INV-09', 'globex', 'paid', 5000, NULL, 'no due date'), ('INV-10', 'acme', 'open', 2500, DATE '2026-12-01', 'last'), ('INV-11', 'acme ', 'open', 600, DATE '2026-10-12', NULL); COMMIT;
statements.fixture_readback: SELECT pg_catalog.json_build_object('database', pg_catalog.current_database(), 'read_only', pg_catalog.current_setting('transaction_read_only'), 'columns', (SELECT pg_catalog.json_agg(pg_catalog.json_build_array(column_name, data_type, is_nullable) ORDER BY ordinal_position) FROM information_schema.columns WHERE table_schema = 'harness_fixture' AND table_name = 'invoices'), 'relations', (SELECT pg_catalog.json_agg(c.relname ORDER BY c.relname) FROM pg_catalog.pg_class c JOIN pg_catalog.pg_namespace n ON n.oid = c.relnamespace WHERE n.nspname = 'harness_fixture'), 'rows', (SELECT pg_catalog.json_agg(pg_catalog.json_build_object('invoice_key', invoice_key, 'customer', customer, 'status', status, 'amount_cents', amount_cents, 'due_date', due_date, 'note', note) ORDER BY invoice_key) FROM harness_fixture.invoices));
statements.case_open_invoices: SELECT pg_catalog.json_build_object('read_only', pg_catalog.current_setting('transaction_read_only'), 'keys', (SELECT pg_catalog.json_agg(invoice_key ORDER BY invoice_key) FROM harness_fixture.invoices WHERE customer = 'acme' AND status = 'open'), 'total_cents', (SELECT pg_catalog.sum(amount_cents) FROM harness_fixture.invoices WHERE customer = 'acme' AND status = 'open'));
statements.case_first_page_by_due_date: SELECT pg_catalog.json_build_object('read_only', pg_catalog.current_setting('transaction_read_only'), 'page', (SELECT pg_catalog.json_agg(pg_catalog.json_build_object('invoice_key', t.invoice_key, 'due_date', t.due_date) ORDER BY t.pos) FROM (SELECT invoice_key, due_date, pg_catalog.row_number() OVER (ORDER BY due_date ASC NULLS LAST, invoice_key ASC) AS pos FROM harness_fixture.invoices WHERE customer = 'acme' AND status = 'open' ORDER BY due_date ASC NULLS LAST, invoice_key ASC LIMIT 3) AS t));
statements.case_missing_values: SELECT pg_catalog.json_build_object('read_only', pg_catalog.current_setting('transaction_read_only'), 'rows', (SELECT pg_catalog.json_agg(pg_catalog.json_build_object('invoice_key', invoice_key, 'due_date', due_date, 'note', note, 'note_is_null', note IS NULL) ORDER BY invoice_key) FROM harness_fixture.invoices WHERE invoice_key IN ('INV-03', 'INV-04', 'INV-09')));

fixture_readback.rows: exactly the manifest rows, in invoice_key order

comparison: Parse the single JSON value psql prints and compare structurally with exact types: JSON strings, integers, booleans and null must match; no numeric/string coercion, whitespace trimming or case folding. 'database' in the read-back is recorded and must equal the bound database name. Any other key, missing key or extra key fails.

case_open_invoices.customer_task: List a customer's open invoices and their total.
case_open_invoices.failure_hypothesis: Wrong rows: a near-match customer (case or trailing space) or a non-open status included, or a row dropped, would misstate what the customer owes.
case_open_invoices.seren_specific_risk: Low for the SQL engine itself; the end-to-end value is that rows written through Seren's connection path are returned unchanged in a separate later connection.

case_first_page_by_due_date.customer_task: Show the first page (3) of a customer's open invoices, soonest due first.
case_first_page_by_due_date.failure_hypothesis: An undefined or wrong order (NULL due date first, tie broken differently, LIMIT applied before ordering) shows the customer the wrong first page.
case_first_page_by_due_date.seren_specific_risk: Low; ordering is fully defined, so any deviation is objective.

case_missing_values.customer_task: Read back invoices whose optional fields were left blank or empty.
case_missing_values.failure_hypothesis: Empty string and NULL conflated, or a missing date filled in, would misreport what was saved.
case_missing_values.seren_specific_risk: Moderate relative to the others: storage and the result path must keep '' and NULL distinct; plain psql -A output would not, so results are JSON.
